definition_checks.derivation: T(x)=x+(O1-O) maps O+t*u to O1+t*u for t>=0. Thus it preserves each ray direction and the convex sector magnitude; the ray at a specified origin with specified direction is unique.
definition_checks.boundary: It maps rays, not necessarily the arbitrarily chosen labeled points A to A1 or B to B1.

definition_checks.derivation: The non-reflex separation of two oriented directions is independent of their chosen common origin.
definition_checks.conclusion: The quantity is an angle magnitude, with same directions 0 degrees and opposite directions 180 degrees.
definition_checks.boundary: The straight endpoint is explicitly required by tasks 481 and 485; no signed-turn or unoriented-line interpretation.

definition_checks.derivation: Translation to a common vertex identifies corresponding same-direction rays.
definition_checks.conclusion: The two convex angles are congruent.
definition_checks.boundary: Parallel supports do not by themselves choose same-direction half-rays.

definition_checks.derivation: For 0<theta<180, the two bounded regions have magnitudes theta and 360-theta; the convex one defines the direction separation.
definition_checks.conclusion: Common-origin representatives give the same magnitude; original differing ray origins are immaterial.
definition_checks.boundary: Connecting endpoints or choosing the reflex region is not the definition.

definition_counterchecks.conclusion: Equal boundary rays do not make convex and reflex regions congruent.

subparts.construction: For M on a side, reuse its support and construct the other parallel support through M when needed. Choose half-rays u,v at M.
On those supports at M choose half-rays -u,-v.

independent_tasks.proof: Translation preserves theta for u,v; simultaneous reversal preserves theta by task 483. The construction works for any M, including M=O or M on a supporting line outside an original ray.
independent_tasks.counterexample: Auxiliary O=(0,0), A=(1,0), M=(2,0): MA points west, not east like OA; do not always use a ray toward the old named endpoint.

ambiguity.description: Not on one side may mean neither side or at least one side. No wording repair is made; the universal construction covers either reading.

independent_tasks.construction: Draw rays AB and CD. Through M take the ray with AB's direction and the ray with CD's direction; choose their convex sector.

boundaries: No numerical value or position of M is required.
Reuse coincident supports while choosing correct half-rays.
Same directions give 0; opposite directions give 180.
The source supplies no nonparallel restriction.
independent_tasks.countercheck: Choosing just one opposite half-ray changes theta to 180-theta.

independent_tasks.proof: The first directions u,v become -u,-v under a half-turn. Translate to the second vertex. Both operations preserve the convex angle, so the angles are congruent.
independent_tasks.independent_check: For unit directions, (-u) dot (-v) equals u dot v.
independent_tasks.counterexample: Reversing only one ray of a 60-degree angle gives 120, not 60.
independent_tasks.boundary: Opposite means each corresponding pair across the two angles; it does not make each individual angle straight.

independent_tasks.proof: After translation to a common vertex, the two pairs are u,v and u,-v. Opposite rays v,-v with common side u divide a straight angle, so theta+(180-theta)=180 degrees.
independent_tasks.counterexample: Reversing neither or both rays leaves theta, so two 60-degree angles would sum to 120 rather than 180.
independent_tasks.boundary: The same conclusion holds if the other corresponding pair is reversed; zero/straight endpoints also satisfy the formula.
